questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the following concepts as used in Algorithms.

(a) Algorithm. (1 mark)

(b) Efficiency of an algorithm. (2 marks)

(c) Sequence control structure. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Algorithm (1 mark).** A finite, ordered set of clear and unambiguous steps that must be followed to solve a problem or to carry out a task.

**(b) Efficiency of an algorithm (2 marks).** Efficiency measures the amount of resources an algorithm uses to solve a problem: mainly the **running time** (number of steps or operations) and the **memory** (storage) needed, usually as the size of the input grows. Of two algorithms that solve the same problem, the one that needs fewer steps and less memory is the more efficient. For example, a binary search in a sorted list is more efficient than a linear search, because it needs far fewer comparisons.

**(c) Sequence control structure (2 marks).** A control structure in which the instructions are executed **one after the other, in the order in which they are written**, with no choice and no repetition. Example:

```text
INPUT length
INPUT width
area <- length * width
OUTPUT area
```

questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe each of the following transmission methods and give an example of each.

(a) Parallel transmission. (2 marks)

(b) Serial transmission. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Parallel transmission (2 marks).** Several bits (for example the 8 bits of a byte) are sent **at the same time**, each on its own wire or line, so a whole byte or word travels in one clock pulse. It is fast over short distances, but needs many wires, is expensive and, over long distances, the bits arrive at slightly different times (skew) and interfere with one another. *Example:* the data bus between the processor and the memory inside a computer, or an old printer cable (parallel port).

**(b) Serial transmission (2 marks).** The bits are sent **one after another, in sequence, over a single line or channel**. It needs only one wire (or one pair), is cheaper and reliable over long distances, and modern serial links are very fast. *Example:* a USB connection, an Ethernet cable, a modem on a telephone line or the old RS-232 serial port.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The administration of a school is made up of 10 employees; each of them uses a personal computer (PC) connected to a local area network (LAN). The network was later upgraded to intranet.

(a) Define intranet. (1 mark)

(b) Give the difference between the intranet and extranet. (2 marks)

(c) State 3 advantages of intranets to the school. (3 marks)

(d) Explain two security measures to be used to protect the intranet. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Intranet (1 mark).** A **private network** belonging to an organisation, built with Internet technologies (TCP/IP, web browsers, web pages, e-mail), that can be used only by the members of that organisation.

**(b) Intranet and extranet (2 marks).** An *intranet* is reserved for the members of the organisation itself (here the 10 employees of the administration). An *extranet* is an extension of the intranet that gives **controlled access to selected outsiders** (for example parents, suppliers, partner schools) through the Internet, usually with a login. So the intranet is internal and closed, while the extranet is shared with authorised external users.

**(c) Three advantages for the school (3 marks)** (any three):

1. Staff can **share files, documents and resources** (printers, a central database of student records) easily.
2. **Fast and cheap internal communication:** internal e-mail, notice boards and circulars, so less paper and less photocopying.
3. **One central source of up-to-date information** (timetables, student results, school policies) that everyone sees at the same time.
4. It is more secure and faster than using the public Internet, because only authorised users can reach it.

**(d) Two security measures (2 marks).**

- **Firewall:** placed between the intranet and the Internet, it filters the traffic and blocks unauthorised access attempts from outside, so that hackers cannot enter the school network.
- **User authentication and access rights:** every employee has a username and a strong password (possibly two-factor authentication) and can open only the files and applications allowed for his or her job; this stops unauthorised staff from reading or changing confidential data such as student records.

(Others: antivirus software, encryption of the data, regular backups, a VPN for remote access.)
